words.note: Divine 神, wisdom 智, study 學: the Greek theos and sophia translated part by part.
The true 真 grain 理 of things. The Society's motto: 沒有比真理更高的宗教, there is no religion higher than truth.
The world as one family, from the Book of Rites. The nearest classical term to universal brotherhood. It appears on page 7.
因 the bed you lie on, 果 the fruit on the tree.
業 deed, 力 strength: what a deed goes on doing.

words.en: rebirth, the turning of the wheel
words.note: 輪 wheel, 迴 to come round.
Things arise 起 through their conditions 緣; nothing stands alone.
靈 the numinous, 魂 the cloud-soul that rises.
魂 rises, 魄 stays with the body: the higher and lower parts of a person.
The three treasures of inner alchemy, each refined into the next.
What a person is before the personality: close to the higher Self. Its partner is 識神.
The everyday, discriminating mind: the personality that 元神 has to outshine.
本 root, 性 what the heart is born with. The same in everyone.

words.en: clear the mind and see your nature
words.note: The Chan formula for awakening. Page 3 shortens it to 明心性.
From the Book of Documents: 人心惟危，道心惟微. The human mind is precarious, the mind of the Way is subtle.
The good 良 heart: Mencius's word for the moral sense one is born with.
覺 learning become sight, 悟 the heart meeting itself.
解 to untie, 脫 to slip off. Mokṣa as taking apart what was bound.
冥 the outer light covered, 想 seeing in the heart.
The plain Chinese name for sitting meditation.
禪 the mind made single, 定 settled under its own roof.
A transliteration, so the readings change: 般 is bān on page 7 but bō here.
Short for 菩提薩埵. 菩提 is bodhi, on page 6.
The first One. It comes out of 無極, the Limitless, and divides into yin and yang.
The shaded and the sunny side of one hill: both have 阝, the hillside, at the left.
合 is a lid fitting its vessel.
The ten thousand things 萬物, one 一 body 體.

words.en: Brahman and the Self are one
words.note: The Upaniṣadic teaching in four characters.

words.en: return to the root, go back to the source
words.note: The direction of the whole liturgy: 返, 本 and 原 are all in the text.
The law that like answers to like.
Wang Yangming's teaching. Compare the refrain's move from 明 to 行.
懺 sees what was done, 悔 turns from doing it again.
The first of the six perfections. 施 is on page 6.
忍 is a blade's edge over the heart.
A life as a commission from above.
Acting without forcing: the Daoist ideal.
What is so of itself: 道法自然, the Way follows what is so of itself.
The Daoist name for one who has become what a human can be.
Heaven, earth and the human between them.

elements.pic: A heart with its chambers. In Chinese the heart is where thinking happens as well as feeling, so 心 is the heart-mind. It stands tall as 忄 at the left, lies open as 心 underneath, and flattens to ⺗ at the foot of 恭 and 慕.
A stone altar with offerings on it. Whatever stands beside it touches the unseen: spirits, blessings, rites, ancestors. As a left-hand part it is written 礻.
A figure with a great masked head. It marks what belongs to the dead and the uncanny: 魂 and 魄 the two souls, 魔 the demon, 愧 shame.
A mouth with sound rising from it. It marks whatever is done with words: reciting, vowing, verifying, protecting.
An open mouth. The most common part of all. It can mean speaking, eating, a person counted, or simply an opening.
An eye turned on its side. Seeing, watching, facing.
An eye 目 on legs 儿: a person who is all eye. Seeing as an act, not just an organ.
An ear. Hearing, and in older thought the gate through which teaching enters: 聖 the sage begins with an ear.
A kneeling person drawn with an oversized head. In compounds it means the head or face, not a page.
A nose. People point to their nose to say 'me', so the nose became the word for self.
Two figures 人 at work 工: the dancers who call the spirits down. It sits at the foot of 靈.
A person walking, seen from the side. At the left of a character it narrows to 亻.
A person standing with arms spread wide: the human being at full stretch. Add one line above and it is 天, heaven.
A kneeling woman with crossed arms.
A swaddled baby with arms out.
A hand with its fingers. At the left it is 扌. It marks what is done by hand: holding, conferring, pulling back.
A right hand seen from the side. In compounds it is nearly always a hand that takes or holds.
A hand with a mark at the wrist, where the pulse is one inch from the palm. It brings the sense of measure and rule: 尊 導 寺.
Two hands lifted together, offering or holding something up.
A hand or claw coming down from above, giving or grasping. It tops 受 and 愛.

elements.en: hand with a rod: to act on
elements.pic: A hand holding a stick. It marks doing something to something: teaching, gathering, saving, pardoning, releasing.
A leg with its foot.
A footprint. A foot planted means stopping; a foot under a line 一 is 正, arriving at the mark.
A crossroads and a foot: going along a road. It wraps the lower left of every character of travel, and of 道 the Way itself.
The left half of 行, a crossroads. It marks movement and conduct: 德 復 後.
A foot pointing downward: arriving, coming after.
A plough, or a flexed arm. Effort applied: 功 merit, 劫 the kalpa, 勸 to exhort.
A cut of meat. In compounds it looks exactly like 月 moon, but it marks the body and its organs: 脈 the vein, 育 to rear.
A person with mouth wide open, yawning or breathing out.
A pair of legs. It carries whatever is drawn above it: 元 the head, 見 the eye, 光 the flame.
A person kneeling. Also a seal, the token of an order.
A person 大 standing on the ground 一.
One stroke. In compounds it is heaven above, the ground below, or the One itself.
Two strokes: heaven and earth, above and below.
The cross of the four directions. Ten is the full count, so 十 also means whole.
The sun with a mark at its centre.
A crescent moon. Take care: a 月 inside a character is often 肉, flesh, written the same way.
Drops falling from the sky's canopy. It tops what comes down from heaven: 露 dew, 靈 spirit.
A current with eddies on either side. At the left it is the three drops 氵.
Flames. Underneath a character it spreads into four dots 灬.
A mound on the ground, or the altar of the soil.
Three peaks.
Nuggets in the earth under a cover. Gold, and all metal.
Three jade discs on a cord. As a left-hand part it drops its dot and looks like 王 king, but in 瑤 理 珠 環 it is always jade.
Tradition reads three lines for heaven, humanity and earth, joined by one upright: the one who connects the three. The oldest form is an axe-blade, the sign of rule.
A field divided by paths. In some characters it is something else redrawn: a head in 思, fruit in 果.
Perhaps a flame, perhaps a grain of rice. White, clear, unadorned.
生 life over 丹 cinnabar: the colour of growing plants. As a sound-giver it carries a sense of clear and pure into 清 情 靜 請 精.
A tree with branches above and roots below.
Two sprouts. It crowns the names of plants, and of things that cover like them.
Two stalks with drooping leaves. Bamboo slips were the first books, so it tops words for writing and answering.
A stalk bending under its ripe head.
Scattered grains.
A shoot breaking out of the soil 土.
A ram's head with curling horns. The offering animal, so it carries goodness: 善 good, 義 right, 美 beautiful, 祥 auspicious.
An ox's head and horns.
A long-tailed bird.
A small bird. It hides in 進 難 離 護 集 雖.
A snake rearing its head.
A cowrie shell, the first money. It marks value: 賢 worthy, 費 to spend.
A tiger's striped head. It tops 虔 reverent and 處 place.
A crowned, coiling dragon.
A roof with its ridge. What is underneath is at home, sheltered, settled: 安 家 宗 宿 寧.
A building open on one side, set against a cliff.
An overhanging cliff. A spring 泉 under it is 原, the source.
Two leaves of a door.
A cloth draped over something.
A wall running all the way round. Larger than 口 mouth, and it always has something inside.
Steps cut into a hillside. When 阝 stands at the left it is this: going up and down, light and shade on a slope. 降 陽 陰 除 隨.
A walled place with a person kneeling beneath it. When 阝 stands at the right it is this: a settlement. 鄰 邪 都 部.
A twisted skein. Thread binds and continues, so it marks 經 scripture (the warp), 緣 affinity, 總 gathering together.
A robe with its collar and sleeves.
A blade. At the right it stands upright as 刂. It cuts, divides and carves: 分 刑 刻 利.
A dagger-axe on a pole, the weapon of a guard.
A bow.
A cart seen from above: axle, wheels and box. It marks what rolls and turns: 輪 轉 載 輕.
A footed bowl.
A sealed jar of wine, the offering drink: 尊 酬.
A lidded vessel of grain.
A net. On top of a character it flattens to 罒. Take care: in 德 the same shape is an eye turned sideways.
A carpenter's square: skilled, measured work.
A hand holding a writing brush. It is in 書 book, 津 ford and 盡 exhaust.
A person lying on a bed. It marks illness.
Perhaps a plough, perhaps a banner. Side, region, method.
A person 大 lying on a mat 囗: to rest on something, hence what a thing rests on, its cause. It gives its sound to 恩 姻 咽 茵.
Something hidden in a corner: lost, gone, dead. Beside the heart it makes 忙 busy; above the heart, 忘 to forget.
The present moment. Over the heart it is 念, keeping in mind.
A banner planted in the middle of a ground.
Two wings turned away from each other. Opposition, going apart: 悲 罪 排.
A mother 母 with ornaments in her hair. It gives its sound to 悔 海 梅 敏.
A bolt of lightning forking across the sky. It is the original form of 電, and with the altar it is 神.
A memorial tablet or a stack of offerings. With the altar it is 祖, ancestor.
Originally a hand holding firm. It gives 持 to hold, 時 time, 詩 poem, 待 to wait.
Threads stretched on a loom, or water under ground. It gives 經 the warp-thread, 輕 light, 徑 path.
A hand turning a spindle. It gives 傳 to pass on and 轉 to turn.
The ground-plan of a cross-shaped tomb chamber. Second, inferior. Over the heart it is 惡.
A saw-toothed weapon, borrowed for the word 'I'. Under the sheep it is 義, what is right.

恩.see: 因 is a person resting on a mat: what you rest on, your cause. Put it over the heart 心 and you have grace: a cause that someone else laid in your heart. To repay grace (報恩) is the heart remembering what it rests on. Historically 因 is here for its sound (yīn, ēn), but the picture holds.
恩.lens: 因 is also the 'cause' in 因果, karma. Read that way, 恩 is karma held in the heart: the debt is not a weight but a relationship that is still alive, which is why the text counts ten of them and pays each one with conduct.

愆.see: 衍 is water 氵 running across a road 行: overflow. Set it above the heart and you have a fault: the heart running over its banks. Compare 懺 in the same title, where the heart stands at the side and looks on.
愆.lens: The fault is drawn as excess, not as stain. What has overflowed can be dissolved (消), which is the verb the title gives it: 消愆.

懺.origin: 忄 heart gives the meaning; 韱 xiān gives the sound. The character was made to write the first syllable of Sanskrit kṣama (懺摩), 'forbearance, asking pardon'.
懺.see: The heart stands upright at the side, as a witness. 韱 means fine, minute (it is the picture of slender wild leeks). Repentance is the heart looking at itself finely, strand by strand.
懺.lens: 懺 names what was done; its partner 悔 turns away from doing it again. Together 懺悔 is the review that frees: seeing clearly is already half the release.

悔.see: Heart 忄 beside 每, which gives the sound and pictures a mother with pins in her hair. Regret is the heart turning back to look. Change the heart for water and it is 海, the sea; for a tree, 梅, the plum.
悔.lens: In 懺悔 the first character confesses and the second resolves. Regret that does not change conduct is only 悔 without 懺's clear sight; clear sight without resolve is 懺 without 悔.

德.origin: 彳 a step, beside the old character 悳: 直 straight over 心 heart. The 罒 in the middle is the eye 目 of 直 laid on its side, under 十: ten eyes find nothing crooked. The Taiwan standard keeps the short 一 above 心.
德.see: Walk 彳 with a straight 直 heart 心. Virtue is not something you own. It is the straight heart in motion.
德.lens: 道 is the road and 德 is walking it: the power of the Way as it shows in one life. The Tao Te Ching is the 道德經. In 功德, merit-and-virtue, 功 is the work done and 德 is what the work makes of the doer.

功.see: 工 is a carpenter's square, skilled work; 力 is strength. Merit is effort that has taken a shape. Nobody hands it down.
功.lens: Set beside 德 it gives 功德. 功 can be counted; 德 cannot. The liturgy asks for both because a deed and the character it builds are two different harvests.

慈.see: 茲 is two skeins of silk under sprouting grass: abundance, growth; it gives the sound. Read as a picture it is a heart with life springing up on it. 慈 is the love that gives joy.
慈.lens: 慈 translates maitrī, loving-kindness. Its partner 悲 translates karuṇā. One gives what is lacking, the other removes what hurts: the two hands of compassion.

悲.see: 非 is two wings turned away from each other: 'not', going apart. Over the heart it is sorrow: a heart that cannot agree with what it sees. Put the same 非 beside the heart and it is 悱, wanting to speak and finding no words.
悲.lens: 悲 translates karuṇā. The character says compassion begins as refusal: the heart says 'not this' to another's suffering.

慧.see: 彗 is a broom: two bundles of twigs in a hand. Over the heart it is wisdom: the heart swept clean. 彗 gives the sound, and it is also the word for a comet, the 'broom star'.
慧.lens: 智 is the light that knows; 慧 is the sweeping that lets it shine. Prajñā here is a removal, not an acquisition, which is why the text says wisdom is opened (智慧開), not given.

智.origin: 知 to know, over 日. The lower part was once 曰, to speak, later written as the sun. 知 itself is an arrow 矢 and a mouth 口: to know a thing is to be able to say it as straight as an arrow flies.
智.see: Knowing 知 with the sun 日 under it: knowledge that has come into daylight.
智.lens: The Chinese name for Theosophy is 神智學, the study of divine wisdom, and this is its middle character.

惡.see: 亞 is 'second, lesser' and gives the sound; it began as the plan of a cross-shaped tomb. Over the heart it is evil: a heart pressed under what is lesser. Read è it means evil; read wù it means to loathe, the heart recoiling.
惡.lens: Evil is not drawn as a rival power. It is the heart put second. Set 惡 beside 恩: the same heart below, and everything depends on what is laid upon it.

恥.see: 耳 ear beside 心 heart. Shame is hearing yourself with the heart; the ear is also where the blush shows. The ear gives the sound as well.
恥.lens: Mencius counts the sense of shame among the roots of rightness. It is conscience as an inner ear: the heart listening to what it has done.

情.see: Heart 忄 beside 青, the green of living things (生 life over 丹). Feeling is what is green and growing in the heart. 青 gives the sound here and in 清 clear, 靜 still, 請 to ask.
情.lens: 性 and 情 are a pair: 性 is what the heart is born with, 情 is how it stirs. Cultivation does not kill 情; it lets it run clear, as 清 is the same 青 beside water.

性.see: Heart 忄 beside 生, life, birth. Nature is what the heart is born with. 生 gives the sound too.
性.lens: 明心見性, 'make the mind clear and see your nature', is the Chan formula for awakening. The nature seen is not personal: 本性 is the root-nature, the same in all.

寧.see: Four storeys: a roof 宀, a heart 心, a dish 皿, and 丁 for the sound. Under a roof, with a full dish, the heart settles. Peace as shelter and sufficiency.
寧.lens: The text values 寧靜 because it is 'good for cultivation'. Quiet is a condition, not the goal.

應.see: A heart 心 beneath a hawk under a shelter (the top gives the sound, yīng). The heart that answers when called, as a trained hawk returns to the hand.
應.lens: 感應, stirring and response, is the old Chinese name for the law that like answers to like: a note struck here sounds a string tuned to it there.

心.see: A drawing of the heart. It never stands for the pump alone: 心 is where a person thinks, feels and intends. When it sits underneath, a character usually names what the heart carries; when it stands at the side as 忄, how the heart is moved.
心.lens: 人心 is the human heart-mind that the text sets out to teach and transform. The old saying pairs it with 道心, the mind of the Way: the one is restless, the other subtle.

唸.see: Mouth 口 beside 念. 念 is now 今 over heart 心: holding something in the present heart. To chant is for the mouth to say what the heart holds now.
唸.lens: 念 translates smṛti, mindfulness. 唸 adds the mouth: recitation as mindfulness made audible.

靈.origin: Rain 雨 above, three mouths 口 (or three drops) in the middle, the shaman 巫 below. The picture is the rain dance: voices raised until what is above comes down.
靈.see: Spirit is what descends when it is called. Three voices under the sky, two dancers at the foot. Keep the three 口 small and even.
靈.lens: The character is a whole doctrine of invocation and response. Nothing in it is self-enclosed: the numinous is a relation between below and above. The simplified 灵 keeps none of this.

神.see: The altar 礻 beside 申, a fork of lightning stretching across the sky (it gives the sound). The power that shows itself at the altar: god, spirit, and also the spirit in a person.
神.lens: In 精氣神, the three treasures of inner alchemy, 神 is the highest: essence refined to breath, breath to spirit. 神智學 is Theosophy.

祖.see: The altar 礻 beside 且, a memorial tablet (it gives the sound). The ancestor is the one whose tablet stands on the altar.
祖.lens: 九玄七祖, the nine dark generations and seven ancestors: the line behind you, treated as still present and able to rise by what you do now.

福.see: The altar 礻 beside 畐, a full wine jar (it gives the sound). Blessing is fullness that comes back from what was offered.
福.lens: The pair 福慧 at the end of the text, blessing and wisdom, are the two things a practitioner gathers: fortune from giving, wisdom from seeing.

禮.see: The altar 礻 beside 豊, a tall vessel heaped with offerings. A rite is the right way to bring something before the unseen, and from there the right way to meet anyone.
禮.lens: 禮 is Confucian propriety, here sitting in a Daoist liturgy next to the Buddhist 戒. The form of an act is treated as part of its truth.

宗.see: A roof 宀 over an altar 示: the ancestral hall. From it come the clan that shares a hall and the teaching a school holds to.
宗.lens: 宗教, 'the teaching of a lineage', is the modern word for religion. The Theosophical motto 'There is no religion higher than truth' sets 真理 above every 宗教.

祐.origin: The altar 礻 gives the meaning; 右, the right hand, gives the sound and the picture.
祐.see: Help from the unseen right hand. 右 is a hand and a mouth: to assist by deed and word. Add the altar and the helper is a spirit.

聖.origin: 耳 ear and 口 mouth above a figure standing on the ground, now written 王.
聖.see: An ear, a mouth, a person standing firm. The sage hears first and speaks second: the ear is drawn before the mouth.
聖.lens: Holiness as receptivity. What makes the sage is not power but listening, which is where every teaching in this text begins.

尊.see: 酋 is a wine jar with its fragrance rising; 寸 is a hand. A jar of wine lifted in both hands: to honour, and the one honoured.
尊.lens: 天尊, Celestial Worthy, is the highest Daoist title: the one to whom the cup is raised.

道.see: A head 首 on the road 辶. The Way is where one goes with the head leading. The same character means to lead and to say.
道.lens: The Way is not a place. It is drawn as a going, consciousness first. 大道 the Great Way, 正道 the upright path, 道心 the mind that walks it.

導.see: 道 the Way with 寸, a measuring hand, underneath: to take someone by the hand along the Way.
導.lens: 引導, to draw and to guide. The Mother does not carry the soul; she leads it, which leaves the walking to the one led.

法.origin: The full old form 灋 had water (level, even-handed), a one-horned beast that butted the guilty party, and 去 to remove. Only water and 去 remain.
法.see: Water 氵 and 去, to go. Law is level like water; a method is the course water takes.
法.lens: 法 translates Dharma: the law, the teaching and the way things are, in one word. 心法 is the part of it that passes only from mind to mind.

佛.origin: 亻 person gives the meaning; 弗 fú gives the sound. It was chosen to write the first syllable of Buddha (佛陀).
佛.see: 弗 means 'not'. A person 亻 and 'not': chosen for its sound, but hard not to read: one who is no longer only a person.
佛.lens: Read fó for the Buddha. The awakened one is drawn as a human being with a negation beside it: what remains when the merely personal is denied.

仁.see: A person 亻 and two 二. Humaneness is what happens between two people; it cannot be practised alone.
仁.lens: The first of the Confucian virtues and the nearest Chinese word to brotherhood: the recognition that the other is of one kind with you.

義.see: A sheep 羊 over 我, 'I' (which gives the sound). The sheep is the offering animal and carries goodness, as in 善 and 美. Rightness is the self placed under what is good.
義.lens: 我 was first a saw-toothed weapon. So the picture is also the offering held over one's own arms: duty as the willing subordination of the 'I'.

善.origin: A sheep 羊 between two 言, 'speech', now worn down to the lower part.
善.see: A sheep over what remains of two mouths speaking: words of good omen, all sides agreeing. Good is what everyone can say yes to.
善.lens: 善智, the good and wise friends of page 6, are the eighth debt: goodness is something one is led to by company.

真.origin: The Shuowen dictionary explains the old form as 'an immortal who changes form and rises to heaven'. The modern shape is 直, straight, on a stand.
真.see: A straight look 直 on a firm base. The true is what stays level when weight is put on it.
真.lens: 真人, the true person, is the Daoist name for one who has realised the Way. The motto of the Theosophical Society in Chinese is 沒有比真理更高的宗教: no religion is higher than 真理, truth.

誠.see: Speech 言 beside 成, to accomplish (it gives the sound). Sincerity is a word that has become fact.
誠.lens: The Doctrine of the Mean calls 誠 the Way of Heaven: reality itself is sincere, meaning it is what it says. A sincere person is one in whom saying and being do not differ.

虔.see: A tiger's head 虍 over 文, pattern. The bearing of a tiger: alert, gathered, still. Reverence as collected attention.

明.see: Sun 日 and moon 月 side by side: the two lights together. Bright; and to understand, since understanding is seeing in full light.
明.lens: The text repays the grace of sun and moon by making the heart-nature clear, 明心性: light answered with light.

光.see: Fire 火 carried above a person's legs 儿: a torch held high. Light that someone bears.
光.lens: 光明, radiance. In the picture light is not a thing in the sky but something a person lifts for others.

照.see: Sun 日, a summons 召 (for the sound), and fire 灬 beneath: to shine on. Sun above and fire below, both lights at once.

普.see: Two figures standing side by side 並 with the sun 日 beneath: all alike in one light. Universal.
普.lens: 普救 and 普照: saving everyone, shining on everyone. The sun does not choose. This is the character of impartiality.

天.see: One 一 above 大, the person standing at full stretch. First the crown of the head, then what is over every head.
天.lens: Heaven is drawn by reference to the human being: the One, touching the top of the head. 天人合一, heaven and humanity are one.

地.see: Earth 土 beside 也, which gives the sound. Change the earth for water and it is 池, the pool of 瑤池. Earth that spreads out and bears.

人.see: A person walking, seen from the side: two strokes that lean on each other.
人.lens: Between heaven and earth, the third of the three powers (三才). The text never lets the human drop out of the cosmic picture.

大.see: A person with arms stretched wide. Greatness is the human frame fully opened. With a line above it is 天; with a dot, 太.
大.lens: The Tao Te Ching names four greats: the Way, heaven, earth and the human. 大 is the human one, standing.

王.see: Three lines joined by an upright. Tradition reads heaven, humanity and earth, with the king as the one who connects them. The oldest form is an axe-blade.
王.lens: The old reading makes kingship a function: to join the three levels. In 聖 the same shape stands under the ear and mouth.

主.see: A lamp stand with its flame 丶. The light a household gathers around, hence host, master, the one who presides.
主.lens: 齋主, the host of the rite, is whoever performs it. The picture says a master is a flame kept burning for others.

母.see: A kneeling woman 女 with two dots for the breasts: the one who feeds.
母.lens: The Golden Mother stands under 無極, the Limitless. A Theosophical reader will think of the Root-substance, Mūlaprakṛti: the Boundless approached as Mother because everything is nursed from it.

子.see: A swaddled infant with its arms free. Child, seed, and the respectful name for a teacher, as in 孔子.

好.see: A woman 女 with a child 子. What is good, drawn as mother and child together. Read hǎo it is 'good'; read hào, to be fond of.

安.see: A woman 女 under a roof 宀. Peace is someone safely at home.

家.see: A roof 宀 over a pig 豕. A household is where the animals are kept and fed: home as a going concern.

宿.see: A person 亻 on a mat 百 under a roof 宀: to lodge for the night. What stayed overnight is 'from before', hence 宿業, karma carried over from former lives.
宿.lens: A life is one night's lodging. 宿命 is what was already written when you arrived; 宿業 what you brought in your pack.

密.see: A roof 宀, 必 'certainly' and a mountain 山: a still place deep in the hills. Dense, close, secret.
密.lens: 密法 is esoteric teaching. The character places the secret in the mountains: hidden by remoteness, not by lock.

冥.see: A cover 冖 over the sun 日, with 六 beneath. The sun covered: dark, the unseen world.
冥.lens: 陽冥, the bright world and the dark, the living and the dead. 冥想 is the modern word for meditation: thinking with the outer light covered.

罪.origin: The older character was 辠: self 自 over the branding iron 辛. The First Emperor thought it looked too much like 皇 and replaced it with 罪, which first meant a fishing net.
罪.see: A net 罒 over 非, what is wrong. Sin here is being caught, not being stained.
罪.lens: What is caught can be untied. The title pairs each fault with its remedy: 消愆, dissolve the overflow; 解罪, untie the net.

解.see: A horn 角, a knife 刀 and an ox 牛: to take an ox apart. From there, to untie, to explain, to release.
解.lens: 解脫, liberation, is the same knife work: taking apart what was bound together. Understanding and release are one word.

消.see: Water 氵 beside 肖, 'small flesh', to dwindle (it gives the sound). Water wearing a thing small: to dissolve.

赦.see: 赤, red (once 亦, for the sound), beside 攵, a hand that acts. To let go: what a sovereign does to a sentence.

救.see: 求 to seek, beside 攵, a hand that acts. To go looking and then act: rescue. Compare 赦: the same hand, a different deed.

報.origin: Shackles at the left; at the right a hand 又 pressing down a kneeling figure 卩. The first meaning is to pass sentence: each act gets its answer.
報.see: Requital. From it come repaying a kindness (報恩), reporting back, and the return that follows every act (報應).
報.lens: The text is a 報恩 liturgy: karma taken up willingly from the side of gratitude. You do not wait to be repaid; you repay.

劫.see: 去 to go away, beside 力 force (去 also hints at the sound). To carry off by force. It was borrowed to write kalpa (劫波), the immense age of a world.
劫.lens: A happy accident of translation: the cosmic cycle is written with the character for a robbery. Time takes everything.

勸.see: 雚, a heron (for the sound), beside 力 strength. Force used to urge someone toward the good. Compare 劫, where the same 力 takes away.

戒.see: Two hands 廾 holding a halberd 戈: standing guard. A precept is a guard kept over oneself.
戒.lens: 戒 translates śīla. The picture is not a prohibition but a watch: the weapon is held, not swung.

齋.origin: 齊, even and level, with the altar 示 set inside its lower half (it looks like 小).
齋.see: To make oneself even before the altar. The fast is a levelling: body, speech and mind brought to one height.
齋.lens: 持齋受戒 is the refrain that pays every debt in this text. The character is tall and symmetrical; find its centre line before you write.

持.see: A hand 扌 beside 寺, which first meant to hold firm (it gives the sound). To keep hold: 持齋, to keep the fast.

受.see: A hand reaching down 爫, a hand reaching up 又, and the thing passing between them. To receive.
受.lens: Add a third hand and it is 授, to confer. Transmission (傳授) takes both: no teaching is given unless it is received.

授.see: A hand 扌 added to 受, to receive: the giving hand. To confer.

傳.see: A person 亻 beside 專, a hand turning a spindle (it gives the sound). To pass along, turn by turn, hand to hand.
傳.lens: With a wheel in place of the person it is 轉, to turn. Passing on the teaching and turning the wheel are sister characters, which is how the text uses them.

轉.see: A wheel 車 beside 專, a hand turning a spindle. To turn.
轉.lens: 轉法輪, turning the wheel of the Dharma. The text says recitation turns the terrace: 轉法台.

教.origin: At the left, tally marks 爻 over a child 子, the same core as 學, to learn; now written like 孝. At the right, a hand with a rod 攵.
教.see: A child at its counting sticks and a hand that directs: to teach.
教.lens: The text joins it with 化: 教化, teaching that transforms. Instruction that leaves the student unchanged would not be called 教化.

化.see: A person upright 亻 and a person turned over 匕. One being, two postures: to transform.
化.lens: Change of state, not of substance. It is the character of alchemy and of every teaching that says you become what you already are.

引.see: A bow 弓 and its string 丨: to draw a bow. From there, to draw out, to lead.

返.see: The road 辶 and 反, to turn over. The road turned back.
返.lens: 返 is the whole direction of this text. Nothing is acquired; something is restored. 返本還原, back to the root, back to the source.

歸.see: A foot 止, a broom 帚 and a mound: a bride going to the home that is really hers. To return, to belong.
歸.lens: The text ends its journey with 齊歸瑤池境, all returning together to the Jasper Pool. 歸 is going home, not merely going back.

復.see: A step 彳 and 复, a foot turning back the way it came. To go back over; again.
復.lens: The 24th hexagram of the Changes is 復, Return: one light line coming back at the bottom. 周而復始, the circuit ends and begins again.

覆.see: A lid 襾 over 復. To cover over; also to overturn. 天覆地載: heaven covers, earth bears.

收.see: 丩, entwined (for the sound), beside 攵, a hand that acts: to gather in.
收.lens: 收圓, the gathering to roundness, is the harvest at the end of a cycle: scattered souls brought home and the circle closed.

圓.see: An enclosure 囗 around 員, itself once the round mouth of a cauldron. Roundness with nothing left outside it: complete.

因.origin: A person 大 lying on a mat 囗.
因.see: To rest on something, and so what a thing rests on: its cause.
因.lens: 因果 is karma. 因 is the bed you lie on; 果 is the fruit on the tree.

果.see: Fruit drawn on top of a tree 木. Fruit, and so the result of anything.
果.lens: With 因 it is 因果, cause and fruit: karma said in two pictures. A fruit takes its season; it is not a penalty.

緣.see: Thread 糹 beside 彖 (for the sound): the hem of a robe, the edge where one cloth meets another, and so the tie that brings people and things together.
緣.lens: 緣 translates pratyaya and nidāna, the conditions that link cause to fruit. Karma is 因果; what lets a cause ripen is 緣. People who meet are said to have 緣.

業.origin: The toothed board on top of a stand for bells and drums.
業.see: A great frame, then the work hung on it: occupation, deed. It was chosen to translate karma.
業.lens: 宿業 is karma from former lives. The picture is a frame that holds what will sound: every deed hung up to ring in its time.

累.see: Things piled up, strung on a thread 糸. To accumulate; also to tie, to tire.
累.lens: 累世, lives strung one after another. The picture is very close to the sūtrātman, the thread-soul on which lifetimes are threaded like beads.

世.origin: Three 十 joined at the foot: thirty years, one generation.
世.see: A world is a span of time before it is a place.
世.lens: 累世因果: the karma of accumulated generations. The same word counts a human life and an age of the world.

界.see: A field 田 over 介, 'between'. The boundary between fields, then the region inside it: realm.

塵.see: A deer 鹿 over earth 土: the dust a running herd throws up.
塵.lens: 六塵, the six dusts, are the fields of the six senses: they settle on the mirror of the mind. 離塵埃 is to leave the dust.

迷.see: The road 辶 and 米, rice, for the sound. 米 looks like paths running off in eight directions. Lost.
迷.lens: 迷 is delusion as a traveller's problem, not a moral one. Its opposite is 悟: the heart recognising itself.

濁.see: Water 氵 beside 蜀, a caterpillar (for the sound). Water with something crawling in it: murky. Its opposite is 清.

魔.origin: 麻 má gives the sound; 鬼 ghost gives the meaning. The character was made to write māra. It is said that Emperor Wu of Liang replaced the stone 石 of 磨 with a ghost.
魔.see: A ghost under a roof of hemp. The tempter.
魔.lens: 降魔, to subdue Māra. In the text the subduing is done by the protector so that awakening can be completed.

鬼.see: A figure with a huge masked head: the dead, seen.
鬼.lens: It stands inside 魂 and 魄, the two souls, and under 魔. 敬顧父母鬼神欽: care for your parents and even ghosts and gods will respect you.

邪.see: 牙, a tooth (for the sound), beside 阝, a town. A place name borrowed for 'slanting, crooked'. Its opposite is 正, upright.

苦.see: Grass 艹 over 古, old (for the sound): a bitter herb. Bitterness, suffering.
苦.lens: 苦 translates duḥkha. 出苦輪 is to get off the wheel of suffering. The same character is the taste of medicine.

辛.see: A branding iron or chisel: sharp, bitter, hard labour. 千辛萬苦: a thousand hardships, ten thousand bitternesses.

難.see: 堇 (for the sound) beside 隹, a small bird: a bird in trouble. Hard, difficult.

甘.see: A mouth with something held in it: sweetness on the tongue.
甘.lens: 甘露 is amṛta, the dew of deathlessness. What heaven sends down is not only weather.

露.see: Rain 雨 over 路, a road (for the sound). Dew is rain that has taken the road down.

生.see: A shoot breaking out of the soil 土. To be born, to live, to grow.
生.lens: 眾生 and 群生, the many who live. In 性 it stands beside the heart: what the heart is born with.

養.see: A sheep 羊 over food 食. To feed with the best meat: to nourish, to rear.
養.lens: The text uses 養 for the earth, for the sovereign and for parents alike. One verb for every kind of keeping-alive.

育.see: A child head-down, being born, over flesh ⺼. To give birth and rear.

修.see: 攸 (a person, a line of water and a hand that acts) with 彡, strokes of ornament. To put in order, repair, adorn.
修.lens: 修行 is spiritual practice. The word says practice is repair: you mend something that is already yours.

行.see: To go, to walk, to do. Its left half 彳 becomes the mark of movement in other characters. Read xíng it is to walk and act; read háng, a row or trade.
行.lens: The refrain of page 3 ends in 行正道, walk the upright path. Insight is followed by walking.

正.see: A foot 止 heading for a line 一: arriving exactly at the mark. Upright, correct.
正.lens: 正道 is the upright path. The picture says rightness is a matter of where the foot comes down.

經.see: Thread 糹 beside 巠, threads stretched on a loom. The warp: the lengthwise threads that stay fixed while the weft crosses them. Scripture is what stays fixed.
經.lens: Sūtra also means thread. Chinese and Sanskrit chose the same picture: a text is something lives are woven across.

誦.see: Speech 言 beside 甬, a tube or bell (for the sound). Words passing through like breath through a pipe: to recite aloud.

文.see: A figure with a pattern marked on the chest. Pattern, then writing, then culture.

書.see: A brush in the hand 聿 over 曰, to speak. Speech taken down by a brush: writing, a book.

言.see: A mouth 口 with sound rising from it. Speech.

證.see: Speech 言 beside 登, to climb (for the sound). Words that go up to be tested: to verify, to bear witness.
證.lens: 證 is also to realise: 證道, to attain the Way. A teaching is verified by becoming it.

護.see: Speech 言 beside 蒦, a hand grasping a bird under grass. To guard with a word: to protect.

調.see: Speech 言 beside 周, all the way round (for the sound). Words that go the whole circuit: to tune, to bring into accord.
調.lens: The text's summary of every scripture is 調和一點心: to bring one point, the heart, into tune.

和.see: Grain 禾 (for the sound) beside a mouth 口. The older form showed pan pipes. Voices and notes that agree: harmony.

合.see: A lid set on a vessel: the two fit. To join, to be whole.
合.lens: 天人合一, 知行合一. Unity in Chinese is a fitting together, like lid and pot.

同.see: A covering over one mouth 口: all under one roof with one voice. Same, together.
同.lens: 大同, the Great Unity: the world as one family. It is the nearest classical term to universal brotherhood.

平.see: A balance at rest. Level, even, at peace.

永.see: A river with its branches: water that runs on and on. Forever. Its eight strokes are the classic exercise for the brush.

無.origin: A dancer with tassels in each hand, the first form of 舞, to dance, borrowed for 'not having'. The four dots below are the feet and tassels, not fire.
無.lens: 無極 is the Limitless: the state before the One. Emptiness drawn as a dance is a fair picture of what the texts mean: not blankness but fullness without edges.

極.see: Wood 木 beside 亟, 'utmost' (for the sound): the ridgepole, the highest beam of a house. Hence the furthest point, a pole.
極.lens: 無極 is 'no ridgepole': no highest point, because nothing has been built yet. 太極, the Great Ridgepole, is the first One.

元.see: A person 儿 with the head marked by two lines: the head, the first, the origin.
元.lens: 靈元 is the spirit's origin. 元神, the original spirit, is the Daoist name for what Theosophy calls the higher Self, as against 識神, the knowing, personal mind.

原.see: A spring 泉 under a cliff 厂: where the water first comes out. Source, original.
原.lens: 原兒 and 原靈, the original children, the original spirits: souls named by where they came from.

本.see: A tree 木 with a mark at its root. Root, origin; and 'this very one'.
本.lens: 本性, root-nature. 返本還原: return to the root, go back to the source.

玄.see: A twisted thread dyed dark. Dark, deep, mysterious.
玄.lens: 玄之又玄, mystery upon mystery, is how the Tao Te Ching names the gate of all wonders.

乾.see: The first hexagram ☰, six unbroken lines: heaven, the creative. Read qián here. Read gān it is the ordinary word 'dry'.

坤.see: Earth 土 beside 申, stretching out. The second hexagram ☷, six broken lines: earth, the receptive. It looks wide and calm next to dense 乾.

金.origin: Nuggets (the two dots) in the earth 土 under a cover; the top, 今 jīn, gives the sound.
金.see: What stays bright in the ground.
金.lens: 金母 the Golden Mother, 金丹 the Golden Elixir. Gold is the alchemists' sign for what does not tarnish: the incorruptible.

瑤.see: Jade 玉 at the left (written like 王) gives the meaning; 䍃 yáo gives the sound. Fine jade: cool, hard, and it rings true when struck.
瑤.lens: In the title jade and gold stand together, 瑤池金母: the two substances that do not decay. Confucius compared the virtues to jade.

池.see: Water 氵 beside 也, which gives the sound. Water that stays where it is. Change the water for earth and it is 地, the ground.

丹.see: A mine shaft with a dot of ore in it: cinnabar, the red mineral.
丹.lens: 金丹, the Golden Elixir. The outer alchemists cooked cinnabar; the inner alchemists kept the word for what is refined in the body: essence to breath, breath to spirit.

師.see: Originally a body of troops and the one who leads it. A teacher is one who leads many.
師.lens: The fifth debt of the text is to the teacher who transmits the method. 大師 is a great master.

賢.see: 臤, firm and capable (an eye and a hand), over 貝, a cowrie, something of value. The worthy: ability that is treasure.
賢.lens: 聖賢, sages and worthies, are the tenth debt: the teachers of every teaching.

敬.see: 苟, careful, beside 攵, a hand that acts. To act with care: respect.

拜.see: Two hands brought together and lowered. To bow.

眾.see: An eye 目 on its side over three people. The many, seen from above.
眾.lens: 眾生, all living beings: the Buddhist sattva. Three people is how Chinese draws a crowd: 众.

民.see: The common people. The earliest form is an eye with a blade at it, the mark of a captive; the word outgrew its picture.

君.see: A hand holding a staff 尹 over a mouth 口: one who governs by giving orders. Lord, gentleman.

皇.see: A shining crown over 王. August, imperial.

父.see: A hand holding a stone axe: the one who works and has authority.

女.see: A kneeling woman with crossed arms.

順.see: A river 川 beside a head 頁. The head going with the current: to follow, to accord.
順.lens: 為人子女順道行: as sons and daughters, walk in accord with the Way. Its opposite is 逆, against the stream.

至.see: An arrow landing on the ground. To arrive; the utmost.

是.see: The sun 日 over 正, upright. What is straight under the sun: right, this, is.

時.see: The sun 日 beside 寺, a hand keeping hold (for the sound). The sun measured: time.

渡.see: Water 氵 beside 度, to measure (for the sound). To cross water.
渡.lens: 渡 is to ferry across: the Buddhist image of bringing beings to the other shore. 渡眾生, 渡原兒.

津.see: Water 氵 beside 聿, a brush in a hand. A ford, a crossing place. 迷津 is the ford where travellers lose their way.

理.origin: Jade 玉 at the left (written like 王) gives the meaning; 里 lǐ gives the sound. To cut jade along its veins.
理.see: The grain in jade, then the grain in anything: pattern, principle.
理.lens: 真理 is truth: the true grain of things. 理 is not a rule laid on from outside; it is found by following the veins.

妙.see: A woman 女 beside 少, few, young. Fine, subtle, wondrous.
妙.lens: 妙 translates sat in 妙法, the wonderful Dharma. 眾妙之門, the gate of all wonders.

利.see: Grain 禾 and a knife 刂: reaping. Sharp; and the gain from the harvest, benefit.

陽.see: A hillside 阝 beside 昜, the sun rising. The sunny side of the hill: bright, yang.

舉.see: Many hands lifting together. To raise, to undertake.

喜.see: A drum 壴 over a mouth 口: drumming and singing. Joy.

盡.see: A brush in a hand 聿 scrubbing out a vessel 皿. Emptied to the last: all, to the end.

共.see: Two hands holding one thing. To share.

親.see: 亲 (for the sound) beside 見, to see. Those you see every day: kin, close. To be near.

存.see: 才, a sprout, and 子, a seed. A seed kept alive: to remain, to preserve.

辨.see: Two 辛 with a knife 刂 between them: to cut between two things. To tell apart.
辨.lens: 明辨是非善惡分: to tell right from wrong, good from evil. Discrimination, viveka, drawn as a single clean cut.

分.see: 八, to part, over 刀, a knife. To divide.

相.see: An eye 目 studying a tree 木. To look closely; and since looking goes both ways, 'each other'. Read xiāng for mutual, xiàng for appearance.

輪.see: A wheel 車 beside 侖, bamboo slips set in order (for the sound). Spokes in their sequence: a wheel.
輪.lens: 苦輪, the wheel of suffering; 輪迴, the turning of the wheel, rebirth.

超.see: 走, to run, around 召, to summon (for the sound). To leap over, to go beyond.
超.lens: 超昇 is to rise beyond. 神超天外: the spirit passes beyond the heavens.

廉.see: A shelter 广 over 兼, a hand holding two stalks. The clean edge of a hall; hence upright, not grasping.

仙.see: A person 亻 beside a mountain 山. One who has gone up the mountain: an immortal.
仙.lens: The older form 僊 shows a person rising. Either way the picture is ascent: the human being who has climbed out of the ordinary world.

忘.see: 亡, lost, over the heart 心. Something has gone from the heart: to forget. Move the heart to the side and it is 忙, busy.
忘.lens: 坐忘, 'sitting and forgetting', is Zhuangzi's name for meditation: the heart letting go of what it holds.

忙.see: The heart 忄 beside 亡, lost. The heart beside itself, losing itself: busy. Put 亡 on top of the heart instead and it is 忘, to forget.

忠.see: 中, centre, over the heart 心. A centred heart: loyal, wholehearted. Stand the heart at the side and it is 忡, anxious.
忠.lens: 忠 is not obedience. It is doing a thing from the middle of the heart, with nothing held back.

忡.see: The heart 忄 beside 中, centre (for the sound). The same two parts as 忠, side by side instead of stacked: and the meaning turns from steady to uneasy.

怠.see: 台 over the heart 心. Idle, slack. Stand the heart at the side and it is 怡, glad: the same parts, a different mood.

怡.see: The heart 忄 beside 台. Glad, at ease. Stack them and it is 怠, lazy.

怒.see: 奴, a slave, over the heart 心 (奴 gives the sound). Anger is the heart enslaved.
怒.lens: Put 如 there instead and it is 恕, forgiveness. One small stroke of difference in the top, and the heart is freed.

恕.see: 如, 'like, as', over the heart 心. The heart that puts itself in the other's place: 'as my heart is, so is yours'. Forgiveness, reciprocity.
恕.lens: Confucius gave 恕 as the one word to live by: what you do not wish for yourself, do not do to others.

忍.see: 刃, the edge of a blade, over the heart 心. To bear: the heart under a knife and still.
忍.lens: 忍 translates kṣānti, patience, one of the six perfections. The picture is exact: endurance is not the absence of the blade.

思.origin: The top was once 囟, the fontanelle, the crown of the skull, later written as a field 田.
思.see: Head over heart. To think is to use both.
思.lens: The character refuses the split between intellect and feeling. Thought is the head resting on the heart.

想.see: 相, to look at, over the heart 心. To see in the heart: to imagine, to think of, to want.
想.lens: 冥想, meditation, is seeing in the heart with the outer light covered. 相 is an eye studying a tree.

意.see: 音, sound, over the heart 心. The sound in the heart: meaning, intention.
意.lens: Before a word is spoken it is a sound in the heart. 意 is thought as inner speech.

志.origin: The top was once 之, to go, now written 士.
志.see: Where the heart is going: will, aim.
志.lens: The will is drawn as the heart's direction, not as force.

息.see: 自, self (a nose), over the heart 心. Breath: what passes between nose and heart. Also to rest.
息.lens: Breath as the link between self and heart. Every school of meditation begins here.

感.see: 咸, all, over the heart 心. The whole heart moved: to feel, to be touched.
感.lens: 感應, stirring and response. 咸 is also the name of the hexagram of mutual influence.

愛.see: A hand reaching down 爫, a cover 冖, a heart 心 and a foot moving slowly 夂. A heart held and carried: love.
愛.lens: The heart sits in the very middle, sheltered. The simplified 爱 takes the heart out.

悟.see: The heart 忄 beside 吾, 'I' (for the sound). The heart meeting its own self: to awaken.
悟.lens: 覺悟, awakening. 吾 is five 五 over a mouth 口, an old word for 'I'. Awakening is not seeing something new but the heart recognising who it is.

惑.see: 或, 'perhaps', over the heart 心. A heart full of perhaps: doubt, delusion.

愚.see: 禺 (a kind of monkey, for the sound) over the heart 心. Foolish. 大智若愚: great wisdom looks like folly.

慎.see: The heart 忄 beside 真, true. Care is the heart staying close to what is true.
慎.lens: 慎獨, to be watchful when alone: the Confucian discipline of being the same unseen as seen.

愧.see: The heart 忄 beside 鬼, a ghost (for the sound). Shame: the heart with a ghost standing by.

怕.see: The heart 忄 beside 白, white. The heart gone white: fear.

怯.see: The heart 忄 beside 去, to go away. The heart that wants to leave: timid, shy.

恨.see: The heart 忄 beside 艮, stubborn, stopped (for the sound). The heart that will not move on: resentment, regret.

愁.see: 秋, autumn, over the heart 心. Autumn on the heart: sorrow. 秋 is grain 禾 and fire 火, the fields burnt after harvest.

悅.see: The heart 忄 beside 兌, to open, to exchange. The heart opened: delight.

恆.see: The heart 忄 beside 亙, a crescent moon between two lines, crossing from shore to shore. A heart that keeps its course: constant.
恆.lens: 恆 is the 32nd hexagram, Duration. Constancy is drawn as a moon that always makes its crossing.

懼.see: The heart 忄 beside 瞿, two startled eyes over a bird. The heart with wide eyes: dread.

慢.see: The heart 忄 beside 曼, drawn out, long. Slow; and in Buddhist use, pride (māna): the heart stretching itself out.

恭.see: 共, two hands holding one thing, over the flattened heart ⺗. The heart under joined hands: respectful.

慕.see: 莫, the sun sinking into the grass, over the flattened heart ⺗. The heart at dusk: to long for, to admire.

念.see: 今, now, over the heart 心. What is in the heart now: to keep in mind, to recollect.
念.lens: 念 translates smṛti, mindfulness. 一念, one thought-moment. With a mouth it is 唸, to chant.

必.see: A stroke drawn through the heart 心. Decided: certainly, must.

覺.see: The top of 學, to learn, over 見, to see. Learning that has become sight: to awaken, to perceive.
覺.lens: 覺 translates bodhi and buddha, 'awakened'. Read jué. Read jiào it is a sleep, 睡覺: the one character holds both ends.

禪.see: The altar 礻 beside 單, single (for the sound). It writes the sound of dhyāna, but reads well: the mind made single before the unseen.
禪.lens: 禪定, dhyāna and samādhi. Read chán.

觀.see: 雚, a heron (for the sound), beside 見, to see. To watch as a heron watches water: steadily, from above.
觀.lens: 觀 translates vipaśyanā, insight. 觀世音 is 'the one who watches the sounds of the world'.

空.see: A cave 穴 over 工, work (for the sound). A hollowed space: empty, sky.
空.lens: 空 translates śūnyatā. Not nothing, but room: the hollow that lets things be.

定.see: A roof 宀 over 正, upright (here written 疋). What is upright under its own roof: settled, fixed.
定.lens: 定 translates samādhi. Concentration is drawn as rightness come home.

淨.see: Water 氵 beside 爭, to contend (for the sound). Clean, pure. Its sister 靜, still, has the same 爭 beside 青.

靜.see: 青, the green of living things, beside 爭, two hands pulling at one object. Contention settled into clear colour: stillness.
靜.lens: 八方寧靜好修行: when the eight directions are still, it is good for practice. 靜坐 is quiet sitting.

知.see: An arrow 矢 beside a mouth 口. To know a thing is to say it straight.
知.lens: 知行合一, knowing and doing are one. With the sun beneath it is 智, wisdom.

識.see: Speech 言 beside 戠 (for the sound). To recognise, to know by marks.
識.lens: 識 translates vijñāna, discriminating consciousness. 識神 is the knowing mind of the personality, set against 元神, the original spirit.

學.see: Two hands working tally marks 爻 over a roof 冖 and a child 子. A child under a roof, taught to count: to learn.
學.lens: 神智學, Theosophy: the 學, the study, of divine wisdom.

魂.see: 云, cloud, beside 鬼, spirit. The cloud-soul: the part that rises.
魂.lens: Chinese thought gives a person two souls. 魂 is light, yang, and goes up at death; 魄 is dense, yin, and stays with the body. A Theosophical reader will recognise the higher and lower principles.

魄.see: 白, white, beside 鬼, spirit. The white-soul: the bodily, moonlit part that stays below.
魄.lens: The partner of 魂. 魄 is also the dark of the moon. 魂魄 together are the whole psyche.

氣.see: Vapour 气 over rice 米: the steam from cooking grain. Breath, vital force.
氣.lens: 精氣神, the three treasures: essence, breath, spirit. 氣 is the middle term, close to prāṇa.

精.see: Rice 米 beside 青, pure green (for the sound). Polished rice: the refined part, essence.
精.lens: The first of the three treasures. Inner alchemy refines 精 into 氣 and 氣 into 神.

梵.see: A grove 林 over 凡 (for the sound). Made to write the sound of Brahma: what belongs to India, to Sanskrit, to the sacred.
梵.lens: 梵 is Brahman. 梵我一如, 'Brahman and the Self are one', is the Chinese for the Upaniṣadic teaching.

祈.see: The altar 礻 beside 斤, an axe (for the sound). To pray, to ask.

祝.see: The altar 礻 beside 兄, a kneeling person with a large mouth. One who speaks at the altar: to bless, to wish well.

祭.see: A hand 又 placing meat ⺼ on the altar 示. To sacrifice, to offer.

禍.see: The altar 礻 beside 咼 (for the sound). Misfortune sent from above. It is the opposite of 福, and the proverb says each leans on the other.

祥.see: The altar 礻 beside a sheep 羊 (for the sound). A good omen: the offering accepted.

信.see: A person 亻 beside their word 言. To stand by what one says: trust, faith.
信.lens: Faith is not drawn as belief in something unseen. It is a person and a word standing together.

孝.see: The top of 老, old, over 子, child. The child carrying the old: filial devotion.
孝.lens: The fourth debt in the text is to the parents. The character draws the payment: the young under the old, bearing them.

謙.see: Speech 言 beside 兼, a hand holding two stalks (for the sound). Words that hold both sides: modest.
謙.lens: 謙 is the 15th hexagram, Modesty: a mountain hidden under the earth. It is the only hexagram whose every line is favourable.

勇.see: 甬 (for the sound) over 力, strength. Courage.

命.see: An order 令 with a mouth 口: a command spoken. Life as what one was told to do: fate, life, mandate.
命.lens: 天命, heaven's mandate. A life is drawn as a commission, which matches 復旨 on page 1: the soul reporting back on its orders.

迴.see: The road 辶 and 回, a whirlpool. The road that comes round: to revolve, to return.
迴.lens: 輪迴, the turning of the wheel: rebirth.

太.see: 大, great, with a dot. Greater than great: supreme.
太.lens: 太極, the Supreme Ultimate, is the first One that comes out of 無極, the Limitless.

全.see: 入, to put in, over jade 玉: jade put safely away, kept whole. Complete, entire.

聽.see: An ear 耳 over a standing figure, and at the right the old 悳: a straight 直 heart 心. To listen is to give the ear and a straight heart.
聽.lens: The right side is the same as in 德. Listening and virtue share a heart. The simplified 听 keeps only a mouth and an axe.

願.see: 原, the source, beside 頁, the head. The head turned toward the source: to wish, to vow.
願.lens: 願 translates praṇidhāna, the vow. A vow is drawn as facing the origin.

晶.see: Three suns 日. Brilliant, crystal. One sun is 日, two stacked are 昌, flourishing.

旦.see: The sun 日 over the horizon 一. Dawn.

暗.see: The sun 日 beside 音, sound. When the sun has gone and only sound is left: dark.

recipes.title: Cause and heart
recipes.note: Above the heart it is 恩, grace. A form with the heart at the side, 㤙, exists only as a rare variant of the same word.

recipes.title: Loss and heart
recipes.note: Stacked, the heart forgets. Side by side, it is busy.

recipes.title: Centre and heart
recipes.note: The same two parts give loyalty or unease.

recipes.title: 台 and heart
recipes.note: Lazy when stacked, glad when side by side.

recipes.title: The lesser and heart
recipes.note: Put something lesser above the heart and it becomes evil. Compare 因 above the heart, which is grace.

recipes.title: 'As' and heart
recipes.note: Forgiveness: as my heart is, so is yours.

recipes.title: Slave and heart
recipes.note: Anger. Compare it with the one above.

recipes.title: Head and heart
recipes.note: Thinking. The 田 was once the crown of the skull.

recipes.title: One and the great
recipes.note: Heaven; and with the stroke lower down, something else.

recipes.title: Mouth and tree
recipes.note: Three everyday characters from the same two parts.

themes.title: The heart in different company
themes.note: The same heart, and what is put above it or beside it.
